transcript: Interview Guide. Activity E. FGD:  Aspirations of Youth
Module 1:  Agency, education and innovation (1 hour)
Most women from our village are living on the second step of the ladder.

Most girls from our village are on the second step of the ladder because all our decisions are made by our parents. We only have rights to few decisions that is why we think we are on the second step of the ladder.
And the girls who got married, they need their spouse’s permission as well as their parent’s opinion regarding anything they want to do. Her decision alone has no value at all.

We are on the second step of the ladder because there are girls who can make their own decisions. However, most girls from our villages are not allowed to make their own decision. They have to live according to their mother, father, and spouse’s etc decisions.
How far a girl will study, who she will marry, even when she will take children, these all decisions are made by her spouse as well as her parents. Her in-laws have a say in it too.
She can‘t go out with any male friend at her own will, she have to tell her parents and can only go if they permit.
We think it is very important to go to school for both boys and girls because education is very essential and valuable. We believe that everyone needs to be educated.

Reason: If we are educated, we’ll be respected by everyone. We won’t have to ask anyone for direction when going somewhere; we can find the place ourselves by reading the signs. If we can educate ourselves we can teach other boys and girls.
If we are educated then no one will be able to fool us because we’ll know what is right for us and if we or someone do anything wrong we’ll be able to right the mistake.

In our area the boys generally study up to class VIII. Their education varies according to their parents financial status. If they are financially well then some boys studies even further. Also there are some who don’t even study at all.
Girls in our village usually study till class V and then they get married. Although there are some girls who somehow manage to pass Secondary School Certificate (SSC).
We think girls should at the least pass SSC and boys should study higher than SSC at least to the level of HSC (Higher Secondary Certificate).

Because mothers can teach their own children as long as the level of SSC, after that education, Boys and girls will be able to travel on their own; they will be able to find places without anyone ’s help. And boys should pass their HSC? Because then their respect will increase in the village, and everyone will take advice from them. Moreover nobody will be able to fool them.

However girls in our village don’t get to study much because most of our financial statuses are not good, and some people thinks that: What’s the use of educating the girls when ultimately they’ll have to go and tend to do house chores when they are married. Moreover some people think that they shouldn’t waste money educating their daughters because the girls will never be able to do any jobs.

In our village, very few people invest equally in education for boys and girls because people in our community don’t know the value of education. Nobody is much interested in providing education for the girls. Parents want their sons to be educated but the boys are not interested at all so eventually most of them ends up with little to no education.
Girls are very much interested in learning and studying but the parents think that the girls won’t be able to do any jobs so it’s a waste of money.
The girls of our village are mostly associated with farming work at home. Girls do all sort of farming work like Eggplants, Cucumber, Paddy, Corns and Wheat.
After the crops are brought home the girls have to do all the work, cleaning the crops and picking the crops, the girls have to do all the work.
When the wheat is brought from the field it has to be dried at home, the girls do this work. Then after frying they have to be under the sun and then it has to be filtered by net.

Girls don’t have to go out and do work when they have babies but they have a lot of work at home. They have to work with corns, wheat and crops. Corn has to be first broken in the machine then have to be kept under the sun for two/ three days and then it has to be stored. Girls do all these works and more.
The main reasons for girls leaving study in our village are:-
Parents force them to get married at a very young age and so they have to leave studies. Most girls get married between the ages of 15-16.

Another reason is some parents may have the interest to continue their daughter studies and the daughters are also interested in studying but they are not financially well enough to do so the girls have to leave studying.
Then there are some girls who are not interested in studying so they leave studying because they don’t feel like it or don’t understand much about what they are studying. So they don’t study.
In many house the girls have to do chores like farming work and they leave studies under the pressure of work at home.
And then some leave studies because while going to school they are harassed by local thugs and they get scared so they leave studies.
The main reasons are:-
Parent marry them off within the age of 14-16
For financial situations. They get to study until its free by the Government and have to leave in high school because often they can’t afford it.
My wish was to continue studies, and to become something big, do a good job.
To be honest we didn’t have any dreams or wishes [laughs]
How can we have dreams or wishes after our study ends, because our dreams would be broken before we could even dream it?

I have to have a particular age to dream, I can dream that I will study a lot and then will develop a dream but how can we start to dream when we have to get married. We can’t dream if we just read till six or seven. You need to reach a certain age to have cleverness, sense of right and wrong; like that you need to reach a certain age before you can start dreaming. In our village we don’t get to reach that age we get married off before that. Then our dreams don’t even get a chance to develop. [9-8 girls also agrees to this]
Normally most girls after they are done studying some work at home, some goes to XX and work at garments, some goes outside to work, wherever one gets a chance they go there to work.
Then again a lot of girls buy sewing machine and work at home. They work at making sweaters in garments in XX.
Some have farming work at home, so they do the farming work at home. They help out their parents with the chores. Many parents are poor so they have to work at their home.
If they get married they have to look after their husband, in-laws and children. They get busy with this.
Many know knitting work so they do knitting work. They make clothes with sewing machine. They make their own clothes as well as others for a payment at home don’t goes out.
In our opinion after girls are done with studying, they should do jobs so that they can establish themselves and stand on their own feet.
In our village, from last year, many new practices have been started. Such as: Corn irrigation, Cucumber, Karala, Sweet Pumpkin.
Before we used to irrigate wheat but it didn’t used to sell much. However now hybrid wheat is in demand so many people irrigate hybrid wheat now.
Wheat irrigation and other irrigation related machine has been introduced. Such as Wheat, Corn beating machine, cutting machine.

Improved medicines have been introduced for Wheat as well for which the production has increased a lot. Other than this, CIMMYT has made opportunities to train the local men in farming and for this the farmers got better knowledge on farming. Although girls don’t go to the training because there’s mostly guys there. The men of the house don’t allow their women to go there. Again we also don’t want to go there because we don’t usually go in front of some men. However some older women go to the training but younger women don’t go to the training.
There are two main practices for women:-
1. Wheat and Corn beating machine is very important for the women because they have to do this alone at home and having a machine makes it easier.

2. Vegetables such as Korala, Sweet Pumpkin is very important for the women because they usually do the farming of vegetables. As they farm their own vegetables they don’t need to buy vegetables from outside.
There are two main practices for men:-
It’s very important for the men to acquire training because if they are trained on how to efficiently grow crops then it will be most beneficial for them.
Then “Shar” (Fertilizer) and “Beej” (Seeds) are equally important because without “Beej” crops won’t grow and to grow good crops “Shar” needs to be used.

In our opinion the youth of our village don’t get the chance to get knowledge regarding new farming ways and wheat. Girls work at their home, men work outside that’s why their works different. Men bring “Beej” “shaar” everything from the bazaar and the women handle them proper at home. They manage the “Beej” and prepare “shaar” for use.

Men plant the “Beej” in the field and women at home puts corn under the sun. Again women don’t get the chances like men because men are the head of the house, if they do anything the women have to pay the consequences.

Girls don’t get to get involve in sale of wheat or any organizations related to it because they don’t go in front of men. Then again if there are no men in some household and they have the field to farm, then they are called to train them so they can farm. Proper training should be given to the women who are interested, those who are not interested should not get any training because there will be no use aferwards.
Module 2.  Gender norms, livelihoods, and family formation (1 ½ hours)
For the women in our villages there are 2/3 new practices for Wheat irrigation:-

Wheat planting machine, Wheat cutting machine and Wheat beating machine. These three machines are brought recently which is very useful for the women because of having this machines it has made it easier for the women.

New improved “Beej” are introduced such as Beej-26, Beej-27 & Beej-28. CIMMYT and people from that office are giving these “Beej” for free for which we are able to use good “Beej” to harvest better crops.

CIMMYT gave free “shaar” and “beej” to the women so that they helped because without “shaar” and “beej” good crops won’t grow so it is very important for the women. The most important thing since the last ten years ago is “Beej” but back then it used to be bought however back then Wheat didn’t grow properly because nobody knew the proper methods ofuse and there wasn’t improved “beej”.
10 years ago women used to use their hands to separate the Wheat by beating them and took help from other people in exchange for Wheat.

In the last 10 years, many improvements have been made in the agriculture practices like many new machines have been introduced which were not there back then. Everyone uses the new machines because its time and cost effective. As less money is required now, the work that used to be done by workers are now done by machine so the cost for the workers are saved. Also new improved hybrids “Beej” are introduced for which production has increased. People from the village farm Wheat-26, Wheat-28 as the production is greater. In vegetables also improved “beej” are introduced such as 40 Sha Karala whose production is much greater.

New agriculture practices has been introduced because CIMMYT’s office people have made opportunities for acquiring new improved “beej” and “shaar”, machine and training for the farming. After few people applied their training knowledge into farming, they realized the outcome is actually good so everyone started the practice and this is how new improvements and changes in agriculture practices have been introduced in the village.

The youth of our village think that in agriculture women have their specific work and men have their specific work. The work for both are separated such as planting corn and giving shaar (Fertilizer) to the field and bringing corns from the field is men’s work.

In the house, the women’s work is to dry and manage them. Also, sometimes the women help out the men at their work but not in works like the works in field. Only in household where there are no men, only those women have to go to the field and do the work.

Also sometimes in some household their might not be husband but there’s sons so then the sons have to work in the field or else society would pass on many ill remarks if there’s men in the house but the women are doing work in the field because nobody likes the idea of women working out in the field.

If any young men tries to grow their own crops and sell it in the market then it will be easier for them. Again, if he can sell in bulk amount of crops from his house then it will be much easier and going to the market would be harder.
He can take a rickshaw van to the market and easily sell it in wholesale there and in this way the young man won’t face any obstacle.
If a young woman tries to grow her own crops and sell the crops in market then she can’t do it because girls don’t usually go to the market because people will pass bad comments about it.
The woman’s husband or son has to take the crops to the market and sell it.
If she grows vegetables then she can sell it by herself from her house to her neighbors.

Women can’t go to the market place to sell any sort of things because, first of all their husband won’t allow them, and then there are many “bad men” in the market place who might tease her. This is the main reason.

In our village it doesn’t happen that way. There is no clear cut division of as such that farming of some plots is the responsibility of some specific members of the household. Everyone will farm collectively whatever plots they have. Then again there are people who have a lot of land they might lease out lands to others to cultivate. And those who has little or no land will cultivate land on lease basis.

The difference between loaning and lending is when you take plot from lending whatever crops you grow, the one third will be given to the land owner who lends the plot. However, another arrangement is taking the plot on lease for two or three years at your own expense and between this time whatever crops you grow will be their own. The owner of the land will only get their land back when they return the money back.
Those who have a lot of land but not enough people to farm only then they lend of those land instead of keeping the plot untouched.
Again some lend of their plots when they don’t have enough money to farm it by themselves. Then they lend it off thinking that they are going to start farming for the next season.

Some also lease out their land in cases where some plots are far away from home so there are many responsibilities and no one to look after this. The cows and goats might eat up the crops and etc so they lease out the plot and keep the plot closer to home for their cultivation by themselves.

Most lands in our villages are is under men’s name. There are few little lands in women’s name. However the women who get lands from their father side have lands in own their name. Also sometimes the husbands also register their land to their wives.

Even when women and men have different lands they don’t specify the farming separately because ultimately the field work has to be done by the men despite it’s the men’s land or the women’s. At home the women have to do all the house work.

In our village even if the husbands write off their land to their wife’s name they don’t give cultivable lands, they only give the lands where the current house is built upon. The logic for this is if and when the husband dies, the wife then have a place to stay.

Everyone works together: men works at the field and the women works at house. This is the norms in the village and the living parents also expect that from each household member. And if any children have their own land then they spend most of their time working on their own land. Then if needed, they work at their parents plot too. However they don’t work much there.
Women also help out men as well if there is too much work at the field, then they finish up their house work then go to the field help out the men in a limited capacity.
The husbands take out the cow and calves to dry land and the wives bring them back. The husbands cut the cow’s grass and bring it; the wives feed the grass to the cows.

The daughters of the household clean the shelter centers for cows. They also do most of the household works. They raise the ducks and chicken. The men don’t think it’s their responsibility to look after the ducks and chickens.

Even if the men somehow do the works relating chicken and ducks only when the wives are visiting their father’s house. Husbands are also shy to do women’s work. Often they fear that people might say like “Hai Allah! The wife is exploiting her husband to do her jobs.”

If a woman is to plant new crops then she will consult her husband about it first. The husband then tells her how to properly do it or if she is to thrash wheat in machine then he’ll show her how to easily do it so the work of the women also becomes easier. She will also have to discuss with her husband and in-laws beforehand if she plans to plant new trees/crops.
If a man wants to plant new crops then he will consult with his wife and mother first like the wife had to consult with him first.

When a women consults with the husband and her in-laws about planting new crops or when a man consults with his wife and mother the results different. Like the woman can only do it if the man agrees otherwise she won’t be able to do it. And if a man wants to plant new crops even though if the woman disagrees he will still do it if he thinks it’s the right thing to do.
Some thinks there’s no difference, the men and women consult in the same way and together. If they do anything together then the outcome will be better.

If Nasima wants to join an institution that grows vegetables like Nasima does at home, then Rafik wouldn’t let her join it. When Nasima and Rafik grows the crops together, and if Nasima wants to join an institution then Rafik wouldn’t let her because he thinks it is better for her to stay home. Whatever they need to learn and know about growing crops Rafik is already learning it from outside.
If Nasima wants to sell her own vegetable Rafik won’t let her go to the marketplace and sell her own vegetables he will say: “No need to go outside rather sell your vegetables to your neighbors.”
If my husband doesn’t allow me to go the marketplace and sell the vegetables then I won’t go there.
If Nasima disobey Rafik’s wishes and goes to the market place to sell vegetables then there will be a fight in the family between the two.
If Nasima goes to the marketplace it will reflect disobeying Rafik even though the sale is good in the marketplace but Nasima still won’t be able to do it.

We don’t think that even though now Nasima is busy with her own activities Rafik will ask for less help. She will have to help out Rafik with his plot’s work first and then she will be able to do her own work.

Not every men is the same, some are different. Some men will say that you can do your own work first and then help me out with my work but husbands like Rafik will say first do my work then you can do whatever work you want to do.

If Mala goes to the marketplace to sell her own vegetables then people’s respect toward her will decrease, the entire village won’t take it in a good way. They will say bad things like: “That woman is walking around the marketplace she’s shameless and have no manner. The village won’t like it at all.”
If a husband stays home and the wife goes to the marketplace the society will gossip about that. They won’t respect that at all and say bad things instead.
Mala’s husband will accept this because this is benefiting their family however the society won’t take it in a good way. They will not respect Mala or treat her well.

If Mala goes to the marketplace and sell vegetables then the people of the village and Monir’s friends won’t respect Monir at all. They won’t value him instead will say bad things like “He made his wife go to the marketplace while he’s staying at home and doing nothing.”
How will Monir have his respect? People will see him and make bad remarks like “He makes his wife go to the marketplace.”
His friends and people of the village will gossip that he’s sending his wife to the marketplace while he’s staying at home.

If mala is successful with her little enterprise, than Manir will like it a lot. But the people from the village won’t like it at all. They’ll continue to gossip and say bad things. They’ll say “ It might be useful for the family but that should not be the reason to send your wife to market place while sitting at home.” Monir will like it because Mala is being successful on her own. Manir and Mala both of them are bringing money to the table which is ultimately helping the family in a better way.
We think if a men and women takes each other’s opinion and permission to do anything then that is equality.
If men and women have same amount of land then that is equality.
Just like a guy is working some place if a girl can work their too then it is equality.
The way a guy lives in the society if a girl can live in the same way then that is called equality.
If a girl and a boy can get equal amount of education then that is equality.
We think gender equality is a good thing however there are many people in the village who don’t think it’s a good thing at all. They don’t approve of men and women doing the same level of work.
Gender equality is a really good thing these way girls won’t be left behind. They’ll be able to stand on their feet.
How much vegetables from Fatema’s garden will be sold and how much will be kept at home for the family, this decision will be made by both Faruk and Fatema together.

In our village we sell most of the vegetables we grow. This decision to sell most of the vegetables we grow is made mutually by both of us. We do this because we think the money we get from selling the vegetables can be used behind for the betterment of the family.

Vegetables don’t stay fresh for much days. That’s why If we don’t sell the vegetables quickly then it will get rotten and if we sell the vegetables then the money made out of it can be used for the family.

If too much of vegetables are grown, then all the vegetables can’t be kept at home, they will get rotten and it is not possible to eat them all at once. That is why selling them is the wiser decision this way we are getting money. This is why we decide on selling them.
Sometimes when the husbands are out and there’s no one to take the vegetables to the marketplace to sell them then the decision of them being sold to neighbors is made.
Faruk will go to the marketplace to sell the vegetables and Fatema will sell them from the house because Fatema can’t go to the market as people will say bad things.
Also when Faruk is not home Fatema can easily sell them to neighbors from the house.
If there is a new farming practice that will increase yield and profits then both of them will do it even if it uses more fertilizer Faruk and Fatema will do it.

They will do this because if more crops grow then they can earn more money and with this money they can buy the fertilizers and new varieties to plant. Ultimately this will be more profitable so they decide on doing this.

How easy or difficult for Diana to purchase the plot of land without David’s support (private rating): 1 = Very easy: 1 vote; 2 = Easy: 1 vote; 3 = Neither easy nor difficult: 1 vote; 4 = Difficult: 2 votes; 5 = Very difficult: 5 votes
Even if the money is Fatema’s Father, she can’t do anything that might disobey her father.

When Fatema got married and came to her husband’s house she have to listen to whatever her husband tells her to do because he have that right. She can’t disobey him at any cost. If Fatema wants that she will do this then it won’t work, she’ll have to take her husband’s permission first.
If Fatema doesn’t listen to Faruk and buys land disobeying Faruk then Faruk will get angry and he’ll tell Fatema to go to her father’s house with her father’s damn money.
Without Fatema’s husbands permission nobody will sell land to Fatema either. Without the husband’s permission buying any land is not a small deal.

Buying and selling lands are not a small deal. When someone will come to buy her land and find out that she don’t have her husband’s permission they’ll think: It’s a deal of a large amount of money, even the money she gets from her father, they will hesitate to sell their land to her if they knew that her husband does not know or she does not have any permission to buy lands.
If somehow Fatema even manages to do this, then there will be fights in the family about money.

How easy or difficult for David to purchase the motorbike without Diana’s support (private rating): 1 = Very easy: 3 votes; 2 = Easy: 4 votes; 3 = Neither easy nor difficult: 2 votes; 4 = Difficult: 1 vote; 5 = Very difficult: 0 votes
Faruk will be able to buy a motorbike easily with his inherited money without Fatema’s consent because he’s the husband and that gives him more right.
Even if Fatema tells him not to buy a motorbike he won’t listen or give much value to her words instead will say “I will do whatever I want.” Fatema won’t be able to say anything more after this.
In our village XX, no young woman can walk comfortably in the local marketplace alone.
Nobody can go anywhere on their own let alone the local marketplace.

They can hardly go to the doctor that too only after wearing hijabs, and only when it’s very urgent to buy something they can go to the marketplace that too only with their mother-in-law or someone else.

Although the places are not much far away they’ll have to wear hijab to go there also even if they are going someplace beside their house they still have to wear the hijab. Travelling without the hijab is not an option at all.

They can’t walk comfortably in the marketplace because there’s too many guys of all sorts t in the market place. People will look at them with ill sight and will gossip about it that “They don’t respect anyone, how they are recklessly walking around shamelessly.” These remarks are passed around.

When a woman get married the change that she has to face is that before marriage she could wear selwar kamiz (a traditional outfit often used for unmarried Bengali girls). She could wear it wherever she would go because she used to go to the school but after marriage she can’t wear selwar kamiz anywhere she goes.

Before marriage a girl can go to the marketplace a little bit but after marriage she can’t go to the marketplace at all. She can only go if her husband takes her with him. Other than that she can’t go anywhere alone.
After marriage if she wants to go somewhere she needs her mother-in-law and husband’s permission.

Given that a women doesn’t have any father-in-law. Her mother-in-law is very sick and her husband is not around. She gets really sick and is in need of immediate medical attention, only then she is allowed to go to the doctor by herself. Other than that she is not allowed to go to the doctor.
The girls who are 7-8 years old only they are allowed to go anywhere they want. If she is older than 10, then she can’t go anywhere alone such as the market place.
Even at nearest marketplace girls aren’t allowed to sell anything. Girls can’t go to the marketplace at all because the people of the society will say bad things.

Out of every 10 women, how many move freely on their own in public spaces (private rating): 1 (practically no women move freely on their own in the village): 2 votes; 2: 2 votes; 3: 3 votes; 4: 0 votes; 5: 1 vote; 6: 1 vote; 7: 0 votes; 8: 1 vote; 9: 0 votes; 10 (practically all women move freely on their own in the village): 0 votes
Reason: They can’t move around alone because the local people will say bad things, will gossip.
They can’t travel alone meaning they have to travel with either brother, husband, father or someone who’s a closely related.
Out of 10 maybe only 2/3 can be considered exceptions.
No unmarried women can go to the city and work alone because her parents won’t allow her. They don’t allow her because if people find out they won’t take it in a good way.
Only if she’s married she can go to the city with her husband and if he wants her then it becomes easier for her to work. Not everyone goes, only the girls who have trouble living financially goes.
The girls who go to the city from our village go only after they are married with their husband.

The girls of our area don’t go abroad to work at the best they only go to XX. That also she has someone with her like a relative or someone, she can’t go alone at all. After going to XX they work at garment factories or work as a maid.
Only because she’s going to the city with her husband her family and friends accepts her back with welcoming hands when she returns to her area.
But if she goes alone then the people back home will say bad things. They’ll say “You went to work at XX huh!.” They don’t see working in XX as a good thing especially if the girl goes alone.
If there is ever a quarrel and in that time she came back from working in XX, they’ll bring it up and will say bitter things about it.
People don’t take it well boys and girls working together. They poke their nose and say bad things about it.
After returning from XX they get work but they have to listen to people’s bad words.
Still she works because she thinks that “Even if people say bad things, it doesn’t matter to me, I need to work and feed myself and live.”
In our village girls usually get married between the age of 12-16 and boys get married at the age of 18-20.
However mostly girls get married at the age of 14. If a girl gets tall enough, dark enough or starts to menstruate then she gets married off.
Boys can marry someone of their own choice. Girls can’t decide who they’ll marry, her parents take the decision for her instead.
In case of boys, mostly the parents make the decisions, the guys can like a girl too.

We think that times are changing now, we live in a modern era where a boy and a girl should have a say in their marriage. Girls can like boys and boys can like girls, they might even have relationships but now if their parents decide something else and marry them off with someone of their parents’ choice then that marriage won’t be a happy marriage or peaceful. That marriage won’t last longer either.
In this generation girls and boys marry someone of their own choice.
It is important to take the boy and the girl’s opinion when it comes to marriage. It is very important to know before marriage that if the boy or the girl have any relationships with anyone.
Also the girl may want to study further so before marriage the parents should talk to the girl and discuss if she wants to marry now or later after studying a little bit more.
In our village when girls get married, within their first year of marriage they have children. Sometimes they have it later but usually by the first year most of them are pregnant.
We think the age the girls in our village of get married is between 14-16. And the age they get pregnant and have children is between 15-17. It is not anywhere near the right age.
Having children at this young age 15-17 is both harmful for the health of the girl and her child. Having children at this age will cause harm to both the mother and the child.

We think the right age for a girl to get married is 18 years old and right age for her to have children is after two years of marriage at 20. This way both the mother and the child will be healthy and safe.

The girls of our village can’t decide alone when and how many children she will have. Both husband wives together make the decision. Her in-laws might have a wish that it’s time for their daughter-in-law to have a child so the girl and her husband have to discuss it with her in-laws too.

Sometimes this also happens that the girls get pregnant unexpectedly without any planning then there’s nothing much she can do. The main reason for this happening is majority people from the village don’t use any protections.
This also happens that I have a son and a daughter and now my in-laws want me to have another child so I’ll have to have another child now.

We want changes like this for the youth of our village; we want that the young boys and girls can study further and get more education. We want that we don’t get forced into marrying at a very young age. We want that whatever happened with us don’t happen with our children.

With permission from the young men and women’s parents, they can independently and properly travel alone and anywhere. Especially girls should be able to travel freely so an environment like that should be made.

Both girls and boys should be able to get proper education and treated equally. If they get educated they’ll be cleverer, they’ll be able to understand what right and wrong for them. Girls will be able to work then.
